title: How to Use AI and Automation in Pumble: API, AI Assistant, and MCP Server
snippet:
The Pumble API addon provides simple HTTP endpoints to **handle** **messaging actions inside your workspace**. It is **available on all** [**Pumble plans**](https://pumble.com/pricing)** to Owners, Admins, and Members**.

This Pumble functionality doesn’t cost any hidden per-user AI markup fees on top of your primary chat subscription. Instead, Pumble uses a bring-your-own-key (BYOK) pricing model, which means the AI infrastructure provider invoices you directly for the raw tokens your team uses. By using a BYOK model, you control your processing infrastructure, budget, and data access policies directly.

For the AI Assistant addon to work, you need to have an active account with a supported LLM infrastructure company.
The live provider support is currently available for Google Gemini and Open AI ChatGPT. Anthropic Claude, Perplexity, and Grok are in the future roadmap.

| **Use case requirements** | **Optimal interface selection** | **Implementation method** |
|---|---|---|
| Scripted notifications, CI/CD pipeline webhooks, server downtime alerts, or rigid cron-job automation posts | **Pumble API** | Standard outbound HTTP POST requests using bearer tokens |
| In-channel brainstorming sessions, direct user queries, or automated workspace thread summaries | **Pumble AI Assistant addon** | Workspace application setup combined with an enterprise provider API key (BYOK) |
| Allowing external software development agents (e.g., Claude CLI) to search code contexts, read chats, and execute commands from your terminal |

title: Pumble API Overview
snippet:
By using the Pumble API addon, you can interact with [Pumble’s API documentation](https://pumble-api-keys.addons.marketplace.cake.com/api-docs/) without using any complex authentication processes. This addon lets you generate an API key that allows you to send messages, reactions, and more via simple HTTP requests.
Info
The rate limit is up to 1000 requests per minute per user.

title: Pumble integration overview
snippet:
[Pumble](https://pumble.com/) is a team communication platform from CAKE.com with public and private channels, direct messages, calls, and file sharing. Persona’s Pumble integration uses Pumble’s **API Keys** add-on to let a Workflow post messages to channels, send direct messages to workspace members, and read a message back by its ID.

Before configuring the integration, you need:
- A Pumble workspace where you are allowed to install apps. The free Pumble plan is enough.
- The **API Keys** add-on installed in that workspace, and an API key generated from it.

### Does Pumble limit API requests?
Yes. Pumble allows up to 1,000 requests per minute per user.

snippet:
limiter

We enforce a rate limit on all API requests in order to maintain high availability and fair usage for all users.
Default limitation is 100 requests per user per minute (per token header) and 500 per app (per x-app-token header).

title: Authorization | Pumble SDK
snippet:
Pumble uses OAuth2 in order to allow your app to access the API.
- User first clicks on a link to Install/Authorize your app. This link can either be through Pumble's `Configure Apps` page or externally through a website.
- This link will open the Pumble Consent screen that will display the scopes that are requested.
- User clicks `Allow`, and Pumble will redirect the user to your `redirectUrl`. Pumble will add a query parameter to this url called `code`.
- Using this code and your `clientSecret` (that is returned when you [create your app](/pumble-node-sdk/manifest.html)) you will be able to generate an access token.
- With this access token you will be able to use the Pumble API.

title: Pumble
snippet:
Connect Pumble with an API key from the workspace’s API add-on to sync workspace members with their roles and status (bots excluded), channels and user groups, and run access reviews. Read-only. Data feeds into your Access accounts and Inventory pages.

- On the Free plan, a free app slot for the API add-on — the plan allows three apps and integrations.
